full_judgment:
Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury, J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh filed by the petitioner, a Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the detenu Zayaan Ahmed Shah, aged about Weight) years, now in the custody of the respondent No. 4, should not be brought before this Court in order to satisfy itself that the detenu is not being held in custody without lawful authority or in an unlawful manner and why the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 should not be directed to hand over the detenu Zayaan Ahmed Shah to the petitioner during the pendency of the Family Suit No. 938 of 2018, now pending before the 2nd Court of Senior Assistant Judge and Family Court Judge, Dhaka and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 The petitioner is the Executive Director of Vision Group, a leading manufacturer and exporter of woven and knit apparels in Bangladesh. She is the mother of one son, that is to say, Zayaan Ahmed Shah, aged about 8, (eight) years and one daughter Zoya Ahmed Shah, aged about 4(four) years. The petitioner and the respondent No. 4 had been in a relationship for several years and ultimately they tied the knot on 26-12-2008. The detenu Zayaan Ahmed Shah was born on 27-11-2010 and the second child Zoya Ahmed Shah was born on 21-5-2014 in their lawful wedlock. Anyway, in the month of January, 2015, the respondent No. 4 suddenly started behaving erratically and became suspicious of the petitioner being unfaithful towards him. Despite the petitioner's reassurances, the respondent No. 4 kept growing more suspicious. At one stage, he became so unstable that he installed, beyond the knowledge of the petitioner, several audio and video devices around their residence to monitor her activities. The petitioner, beginning to sense an obvious change in the behaviour, demeanour and mental state of the respondent No. 4, and being wary of how it began to affect their marriage and the lives of their children, informed her in-laws of his condition. The respondent No. 4, prior to this mental breakdown, did never show any visible sign of mental disequilibrium. His parents were divorced in 2002, and have since been living in separate jurisdictions. The respondent No. 4 was taken to various medical institutes in Thailand, United Kingdom, Spain and Canada. He was eventually diagnosed with Delusional Disorder/Schizophrenia in several medical facilities and received treatment in rehabilitation centres for over three years. Besides, the respondent No. 4 is a drug addict. Despite such diagnosis, he refused to take medication and started abusing his wife (petitioner) resulting in severe psychological trauma to her. Because of the unpredictable and unstable mental state of the respondent No. 4, the petitioner diligently took care of the minor children as well as ensured proper treatment for the respondent No. 4 both at home and abroad. The petitioner under-took the responsibility to care for her family with the unstinted support from her parents. They have been actively involved with the raising of the children and providing necessary care to them at every possible stage, both financially and emotionally. After 10(ten) years of marriage, the petitioner was forced to return to her paternal house with the two minor children. However, the respondent No. 4 maintained periodic contacts with the petitioner and the children and met them from time to time. He would also take the children out occasionally and return them safely to the petitioner during the period of estrangement. She always tried her level best to shield her minor children from the negative effects of the marital dispute between her and the respondent No. 4. 

 4. At one stage, the petitioner filed Family Suit No. 938 of 2018 before the 2nd Court of Senior Assistant Judge and Family Court Judge, Dhaka for the custody of the detenu Zayaan Ahmed Shah and the daughter Zoya Ahmed Shah. The daughter Zoya Ahmed Shah is currently in the custody of the petitioner. The petitioner is in possession of the Bangladeshi Passport being No. BF0900800 of the detenu and filed General Diary (GD) Entry No. 294 dated 5-11-2018 with Gulshan Police Station, DIM; Dhaka in order to prevent a new passport from being issued in favour of the detenu. The purpose of the GD was to preclude the respondent No. 4 from taking the detenu unlawfully out of the country without informing the petitioner. Furthermore, the respondent No. 4 and the detenu were granted permanent residence cards in Canada. Therefore, the petitioner is at serious risk of losing all access to her only son since there is a strong likelihood that the respondent No. 4 will attempt to leave the jurisdiction of this Court with the detenu. However, the petitioner is currently residing with her parents at their residence. She is financially capable of taking care of both the minor children. Moreover, she has full support of her parents who are financially affluent too. There is enough space and accommodation at their residence for both the children of the petitioner. The mother of the petitioner is a home-maker and has also been active as a grandmother in supporting her daughter in every possible way and in taking care of her grandchildren. As the detenu Zayaan Ahmed Shah was taken out of the custody of the mother-petitioner illegally, the Rule is liable to be made absolute and a direction may be given upon the respondent No. 4 to hand over the custody of the detenu to her within a given time-frame. 

 The Writ Petition was filed with the malafide intention of harassing and humiliating the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 and the interim directions were obtained by the petitioner by misleading the Court and suppressing some material facts. The respondent Nos. 4 and 5 were staying abroad at the time of filing the Writ Petition. Nevertheless the petitioner gave a fake impression to the Court that the respondent No. 4 along with the detenu was likely to leave the jurisdiction of the Court. She was fully aware that the respondent No. 4 went to Indonesia for holidays along with his son Zayaan Ahmed Shah on 8-11-2018. But she deliberately did not state that fact in the Writ Petition. The petitioner further suppressed that the respondent No. 4 filed a Family Suit being No. 931 of 2018 before the 2nd Court of Senior Assistant Judge and Family Court Judge, Dhaka on 25-10-2018 claiming guardianship of the minor children, namely, Zayaan Ahmed Shah and Zoya Ahmed Shah. The petitioner also suppressed that she filed a Family Suit being No. 937 of 2018 before the 5th Court of Additional Assistant Judge and Family Court Judge, Dhaka on 5-11-2018 for restitution of conjugal rights. Ultimately the Family Suit No. 937 of 2018 was withdrawn by the petitioner and the divorce between the petitioner and the respondent No. 4 had already become effective. The petitioner also suppressed that the respondent No. 4 filed a Petition Case being No. 352 of 2018 before the learned Executive Magistrate, Narayanganj on 6-11-2018 for recovery of valuable documents like Passports, Canadian Permanent Residence Cards, Health Cards etc. of the respondent No. 4 and Zayaan. The petitioner has raised a catena of allegations against the respondent No. 4 in the Writ Petition which are highly contentious/disputed. So the Writ Petition is not maintainable. 

 6. It is denied that on 1340-2018, the detenu Zayaan Ahmed Shah was unlawfully taken away by the respondent No. 4 under false pretences and that despite several attempts of the petitioner, the child has been wrongfully kept under his custody depriving her of all access or visitation rights. It is stated that the audio and video devices were installed at their matrimonial residence at her own instance. Since 2015, the petitioner's behaviour and attitude towards the respondent No. 4 changed dramatically. From that particular period, she started behaving with him mysteriously. He took up the matter with her in confidence and tried to iron out the misunderstandings between them. But she failed to cooperate with him in this regard. This gradually gave rise to mutual distrust between them. At one point of time, the petitioner became very desperate and accustomed to an unruly and indecent lifestyle. Thereafter, she developed an extra-marital relationship with a stranger. The petitioner, her mother and sisters carefully orchestrated the drama of mental disequilibrium of the respondent No. 4 and stigmatized him as a psychiatric patient. In fact, as part of a deep-rooted plot, the petitioner prompted the respondent No. 4 to install the audio and video devices (keeping the devices under her absolute control) in order to establish and prove that the respondent No. 4 has been suffering from some kind of abnormal delusion resulting in severe paranoia. The alleged desperate attempt of the so-called "devoted wife" (petitioner) to get the respondent No. 4 "the best possible medical treatment" is highly motivated, pre-planned and an out-and-out after thought and is designed to suit her mala fide intention. The respondent No. 4 was never a psychiatric patient or a schizophrenic that required medical treatment at any rehabilitation centre for the alleged period of 3(three) years. The contents of the so-called medical certificates and diagnostic reports are all manufactured/ fabricated. Whether the respondent No. 4 has mental incapacity/ disability or not is a highly contentious/ disputed question of fact which cannot be adjudicated upon by the High Court Division in its writ jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution. In order to determine the mental health of a person, there is a set statutory procedure as delineated in মানসিক স্বাস্থ্য আইন, ২০১৮. But no step was taken on behalf of the petitioner to take necessary steps in accordance with the provisions of মানসিক স্বাস্থ্য আইন, ২০১৮ to declare the respondent No. 4 as a psychiatric patient. The respondent No. 4 with great patience all along tried to cope with the changed behaviour of the petitioner and also tried to make her understand that for the greater interest and welfare of the children, the matrimonial relationship should not be impaired further. Despite all efforts on the part of the respondent No. 4, the petitioner failed to rectify herself in consequence of which the matrimonial relationship between them suffered a jolt and eventually it fell apart. In such a situation, the petitioner went abroad for a while and came back on 4-5-2018. Afterwards, the respondent No. 4 was forced to rent a room in Lakeshore Hotel, Dhaka which was nearer to his father-in-law's house. On 8-10-2018, the respondent No. 4 brought the petitioner and the children in his paternal house, namely, "Sobhan Manzil" situated at Fatullah, Narayanganj. But in the absence of the respondent No. 4, the petitioner surreptitiously took away all valuable personal documents of the respondent No. 4 and his son Zayaan Ahmed Shah and daughter Zoya Ahmed Shah. Consequently the respondent No. 4 was constrained to lodge a GD Entry being No. 121 dated 3-11-2018 with Fatullah Police Station, Narayanganj. Sub-sequently, the respondent No. 4 filed a complain case being No. 352 of 2018 against the petitioner in the Court of the Executive Magistrate, Narayanganj which is still pending for disposal. 

 9. In the Affidavit-in-Reply, it has been stated that it came to the knowledge of the petitioner, after three weeks of the deceitful removal of the detenu from her custody, that the respondent No 4 was leaving the jurisdiction with the detenu on 8-11-2018 after receiving an instant message and photograph from a friend who had spotted them at the airport at the time of their departure. Then and there, the petitioner rushed to the airport and sorted out the detenu with the respondent No, 4. The respondent No. 4 then produced a return ticket and assured the petitioner as well as the Officer-in-Charge (Immigration) at the Ha rat Shahjalal International Airport, Dhaka that he would return to Bangladesh by 18-11-2018, that is to say, prior to filing of the instant Writ Petition. It is vehemently denied that the petitioner attempted to suppress the facts before the Court since she had lost all contacts with the detenu and the respondent No. 4 immediately after their departure from Bangladesh and she had the belief that they would return to Bangladesh on 18-11-2018 as per the return ticket. It was the apprehension of losing her son that led her to file the instant Writ Petition a day after their expected arrival for an immediate relief. As the Family Stilt No. 937 of 2018 was already withdrawn, it was not required to be brought to the notice of the Court. The detenu was not only deceitfully removed from the custody of the petitioner, but also he was taken out of the jurisdiction of Bangladesh by the respondent No. 4 without her consent thereby depriving her of all physical access to her only, son. She had no knowledge about the installation of the audio and video devices around their house until much later. She was always faithful to the respondent No. 4 and she did never develop any extramarital relationship with any stranger as asserted on behalf of the respondent No. 4. It is widely understood and expected that in a proceeding involving the custody of minor children, an attempt is always made to assassinate the character of the mother, painting her as the most unfit mother to care for her children, despite the reality of the situation and the devotion of the mother. As such, the allegations levelled against the petitioner by the respondent No. 4 are all wild allegations. The petitioner only wishes to establish the incapacity and incapability of the respondent No. 4 to take care of the detenu and does not wish to obtain an evaluation or declaration as regards him as a mentally disabled person or a schizophrenic. There was no justification on the part of the respondent No. 4 for his stay in a hotel, at one point of time, for better communication with the children. It is a feeble attempt to cover up an obvious pattern of his paranoia which speaks volumes about his erratic behaviour and mental disequilibrium. If the welfare of the child is of paramount consideration, surely it cannot be ensured while the detenu is in the custody of the respondent No. 4. 

 10. The respondent No. 4, according to the statements made in the Affidavit-in-Opposition, has several businesses to attend to, and hence, he is, arguably, extremely busy. Therefore, it is quite impossible for him to give enough care and attention to the detenu, a boy of 8(eight) years, who needs round-the-dock parenting, mentoring and attention. In this perspective, the welfare of the detenu cannot be ensured while he is in the custody of the respondent No. 4. Besides, the respondent No. 4 himself is a member of a broken family. His mother is a resident of Canada and only periodically visits Bangladesh. He seems to live separately from his father and step-mother who reside in Bangladesh. Owing to this, and his busy schedule, it will be impossible for him to provide the detenu with necessary care, affection and support. The detenu, while in the custody of the petitioner, had consistent supervision of either the petitioner, or in her absence, her parents or sister. This kind of familial support and cordial upbringing, whilst in the care of the petitioner, will be very difficult on the part of the respondent No. 4 to provide, given the current state of his life. It is crucial that the detenu, after such a long time away from his education and a normal life, is given intensive care at home, and not left in the sole care of hired nannies and caregivers. The petitioner has never had any suicidal tendencies and is a perfectly stable individual, unlike the respondent No. 4. Further, the medical report of the petitioner produced by the respondent No. 4 is misleading. They were having a lot of marital incompatibilities during the period preceding 22-6-2017, the day on which she was admitted to the United Hospital, Dhaka. The petitioner, a few days prior to the admission, was under tremendous mental pressure from the respondent No. 4 to admit to the alleged conjugal infidelity. He appeared to have been experiencing one of his psychotic episodes, as he refused to allow her to go anywhere or to do anything, and thereby created a hostile atmosphere at home. Out of frustration resulting from constant mental pressure, she took a few diazepam tablets to reduce her anxiety and stress in order to get some sleep. The petitioner's report of ultra-sonogram dated 13-10-2009 was fraudulently taken out of context and presented before the Court as a report of 'cutting her veins'. Actually she was diagnosed with viral fever and had been admitted to the United Hospital from 25-9-2009 to 30-9-2009. On 7-10-2009 and 13-10-2009, she was further diagnosed with Phlebothrombosis with Thrombophlebitis (left upper limb). So the question of commission of suicide by her as alleged is out of the question. The welfare of the detenu will be far better protected by being in the custody of the petitioner during the pendency of the Family Suit Nos. 931 of 2018 and 938 of 2018. 

 11. At the outset, Mr Reshad Imam, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the mother-petitioner, submits that the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 in their Affidavit-in-Opposition, in a desperate attempt to malign the character of the petitioner, has made some wild, unfounded and uncorroborated allegations against her to mislead the Court about her alleged conjugal infidelity; but she has produced some credible evidence from reputed foreign institutions as to the mental state of the respondent No. 4 which ought to be taken into account in deciding the interim custody of the detenu. 

 12. Mr Reshad Imam also submits that the petitioner does not seek any declaration with regard to the mental health of the respondent No. 4; but she has a duty to present all the relevant facts for consideration before the Court for proper and effectual adjudication of the Rule and considered from this angle, the question of following the procedure as contemplated by মানসিক স্বাস্থ্য আইন, ২০১৮ is immaterial. 

 17. Mr Reshad Imam also submits that even if the medical reports of the respondent No. 4 as evidenced by Annexure 'B' series to the Writ Petition are thrown to the winds for the sake of argument, yet there are other relevant factors which need to be considered by the Court in deciding with whom the welfare of the detenu lies particularly when it has been admitted in paragraph 17 of the Affidavit-in-Opposition filed by the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 that the respondent No. 4 is an extremely busy individual holding important positions in various companies and this is why, it would be well-nigh impossible for the respondent No. 4 to devote enough time and attention to the detenu to ensure his healthy upbringing and given this landscape, the custody of the detenu Zayaan Ahmed Shah should be restored to the petitioner during the pendency of the two Family Suits. 

 24. The alleged mental disequilibrium or instability of the respondent No. 4 and the alleged conjugal infidelity of the petitioner are all matters of evidence and trial being disputed questions of facts. Since these are disputed questions of facts, the same cannot be appreciated in this writ proceeding under Article 102 of the Constitution. If this Division accepts the contention of either party in this regard, that will amount to begging the question. However, the Family Court in the pending Family Suits will decide conclusively the questions of custody and guardianship of the minor children on the basis of the evidence to be adduced by the parties during the trial of those Family Suits. But none the less, this writ Court can decide the interim custody of the detenu Zayaan Ahmed Shah in the light of the 'ratio' enunciated by the Appellate Division in the decision in the case Of Abdul Jaill and others vs Sharon Laily Begunt Jalil reported in 50 DLR (AD) 55 relied upon by Mr Reshad Imam. 

 25. Leaving aside the contentious/ disputed questions of facts in this case, we may proceed to determine the interim custody of the detenu solely on the basis of the admitted facts. The admitted facts are that the detenu Zayaan Ahmed Shah had been in the custody of the petitioner following her estrangement from the respondent No. 4 and the detenu was removed from her custody on 13-10-2018 and was never returned to her thereafter. Besides, the respondent No. 4 did not obtain the consent of the petitioner for having the custody of the detenu. What is more, the respondent No. 4 did not obtain any order from the Family Court with regard to the interim custody of the detenu. What we are driving at boils down to this without the consent of the petitioner and by keeping the Family Court in the dark, the respondent No. 4 secured the custody of the detenu Zayaan Ahmed Shah on 13-10-2018 unlawfully and the detenu has been in his custody till date. The Family Suit No. 931 of 2018 was filed by the respondent No. 4 for the custody and guardianship of the minor children Zayaan Ahmed Shah and Zoya Ahmed Shah. On the other hand, the petitioner filed the Family Suit No. 938 of 2018 against the respondent No. 4 for the custody and guardianship of the minor children. 130th the suits are still pending for adjudication before the 2nd Court of Senior Assistant Judge and Family Court Judge, Dhaka. 

 "33. It is true that the High Court Division gave no consideration, not to speak of making any finding, to the story of alleged deceitful removal of the children on 8-5-95 by the appellant father nor was it held that the custody of the appellant was for any reason unlawful. But then we find substance in the submission of Dr. Hossain that normally the minor children should be with their mother as long as she does not earn any disqualification for such custody and if there is a breach of this normal order brought about by an unilateral act of the father or anybody on his behalf, the aggrieved mother has the right to move the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution for immediate custody of the children which may be ordered in the interest and for the welfare of the said children." 

 9. A petition in this nature of habeas corpus for the custody of a minor would also be equally competent without sending the petitioner to exhaust his or her remedy before the Family Court under the Guardians and Wards Act or other Criminal Court which is neither expedient nor an equally efficacious remedy in a situation like this and, in fact, a habeas corpus petition would give her the most speedy and efficacious remedy." 

 "In all actions concerning children, whether undertaken by public or private social welfare institutions, courts of law, administrative authorities or legislative bodies, the best interests of the child shall be a primary consideration." 

 "10. These decisions, while recognizing the principle of Islamic Law as to who is entitled to the custody of a minor son with reference to his or her age and sex, simultaneously took into consideration the welfare of the minor child in determining the question. Courts in all these cases, seemed reluctant to give automatic effect to the rule of Hizanat enunciated by Islamic jurists. If circumstances existed which justified the deprivation of a party of the custody of his child to whose custody he was entitled under Muslim Law, Courts did not hesitate to do so. It may be argued, as the appellant's Counsel did, that the welfare of the child would be best served if his custody is given to a person who is entitled to such custody. Nevertheless, the Court's power to determine the entitlement of a party to the Hizanat is not limited to mere observance of age rule so as to exclude the consideration of the interest of the child which would, however, depend on the facts and circumstances of a given case." 

 32.  From the forgoing discussions, it is manifestly clear that the welfare of the minor children is of paramount consideration in determining their custody. Even the Rule of Hizanat may be given a go-by by the Court in an appropriate case depending upon its facts and circumstances. In this respect, no strait-jacket formula can be laid down. 

 33. Reverting to the case in hand, as observed earlier, admittedly the detenu had been in the custody of the mother-petitioner till 12-10-2018 and on 13-10-2018, the father-respondent No. 4 took away the detenu from the custody of the petitioner for some reason or another and since then, the detenu has been in his custody. It is also admitted that the respondent No. 4 did not obtain the consent of the petitioner with regard to the custody of the detenu under him. On top of that, undeniably the respondent No. 4 did not seek the intervention of the Family Court for the interim custody of the detenu to meet the emergent situation which allegedly arose at the relevant point of time resulting from the purported conjugal infidelity and extra-marital relationship of the petitioner. This being the panorama, we are of the view that the detenu was illegally removed from the custody of the petitioner by the respondent No. 4 on 13-10-018. 

 36. the most striking phenomenon is that on 13-10-2018, the respondent No. 4 took away the detenu Zayaan Ahmed Shah from the custody of the petitioner without her consent and the intervention of the Family Court. So from this standpoint alone, the custody of the detenu must be restored to the petitioner during the pendency of the Family Suits. In other words, the "status-quo ante" must be restored vis-a-vis the. Custody of the detenu during the pendency of the Family Suits. 

 39. Be that as it may, the observations and findings arrived at in this judgment will have no bearing upon the merit of the Family Suits pending before the Family Court below. The Family Court will independently assess the merit of both the Family Suit Nos. 931 of 2018 and 938 of 2018 and dispose of the same in accordance with law. 

 41. The father-respondent No. 4 is hereby directed to hand over the detenu Zayaan Ahmed Shah, aged about 8(eight) years, to the custody of the mother-petitioner Sarah Hamid at the house of Mr Reshad Imam, learned Advocate for the mother-petitioner, being No. 51/A (Apartment No. C-1), Road No. 6/A (New), Dhartmondi Residential Area, Dhaka at a conveniently agreed time within 7(seven) days from date. The father-respondent No. 4 will have the right to visit the minor children, namely, Zayaan Ahmed Shah and Zoya Ahmed Shah at a conveniently agreed time, place and period twice a week. In case of any disagreement in this respect, the parties will be at liberty to seek necessary directions from the Family Court. 

 42. The 2nd Court of Senior Assistant Judge and Family Court Judge, Dhaka is, however, directed to dispose of the Family Suit Nos. 931 of 2018 and 938 of 2018 analogously as expeditiously as possible preferably within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment. 

 Let a copy of this judgment be immediately transmitted to the 2nd Court of Senior Assistant Judge and Family Court Judge, Dhaka for information and necessary action.
